title: Ibn al-Qubabi's cipher verse in a Mamluk secretary's book of cipher correspondence, Penn LJS 51 f. 106v

documents.shelfmark: University of Pennsylvania, Kislak Center, LJS 51, f. 106v (OPenn image 0084_0217)

plaintext.source: The compiler's solution followed on the next leaf, which is lost; only three or four red letters over line 1 (a later reader's partial gloss, partly wrong). No edition or study found (15 Nov 2026).

transcription.source: OPenn master TIFF 2339 x 2959 px, line crops at 1.5x and 2.2x, checked against connected components of the ink
transcription.notes: 22 words with dividers. Joined glyphs (E, P, Z family) and near-identical pairs (A/B, U/T, round 8 versus angular alif in line 6) were settled on the components; line 1 word 2 is abraded.

system.summary: Invented signs for the Arabic letters, word dividers kept, read right to left, with more than one sign for the commonest letters.
system.notes: The facing page describes the same circle's tricks: lam-alif as one sign, writing left to right, nulls added at the end. Homophones: two signs for lam (M, A) and for ha (D, Q); alif probably more than one (H, Z).

prior_solution.where: The compiler solved it at once ("fa-halaltuha fi l-hal bi-hudurihi"), but his solution was on the next leaf, which is lost; a later reader glossed five signs in red, partly wrong. No modern reading found (Penn record, Digital Scriptorium, web searches in English and Arabic, Tomokiyo, Lasry, DECODE; 15 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: asked for an Arabic sweep, then set the goal 'solve LJS 51 f. 106v' with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Found in the Arabic sweep; downloaded the OPenn master TIFF of f. 106v and the facing pages.
Transcribed seven lines sign by sign (90 signs, 22 words) and checked the segmentation on connected components of the ink.
One-to-one keys, both reading directions, with and without a lam=alif shared sign, scored by a new classical Arabic poetry 5-gram model.
Fixed the red-gloss values over line 1 (waw, ta, alif, ghayn, sin).
With alif fixed on the commonest sign, the annealer read the two words sharing NHYKHM as wa-amthaluka / wa-amthaluha, giving waw, alif, mim, tha, lam, ha; then humam, ayda, kun, himmatuk, wa-minka.

Homophones for the frequent letters (two lams, two has, extra alif signs), suggested by laha/mayl and huwa/wa-amthaluhu; supported by the compiler's own preface (f. 7v, image 0014: 'the letter is one, the shapes differ').
Word-level beam search against the corpus vocabulary; real words but no single coherent key while eight signs occur once.
Metre: both line ends scan as tawil (rhyme -ayda); the second line's 'wa-amthaluhu humam' resists tawil.
Template-matched seven distinctive signs over the volume's other 210 pages to find the alphabet reused with a plaintext; no reuse.
From the compiler's note 'ja'ala al-lam alifan': the alif sign also stands for lam. The annealer then reads wa-li-l-nasi amthalun, aqulu, li-l-hajri.
Tawil scansion by a second reader: wa-li-l-nasi amthalun scans; the skeleton still fails the metre at w3, w8-w9 and w20, so no complete reading is accepted.
Scored each bayt without the dividers: S read as alif, giving wa-ma kulluha ayda and wa-la li-l-hija' wa-amthaluha ayda.
Dividers placed one sign late after kaf (twice); with them moved, line 1 ends huma kanu wa-ma kulluha ayda.

Tawil scansion of the updated skeleton: bayt 1 scans in full (wa-li-l-husni amthalun ka-amyala li-l-hawa ... hawanun huma kanu wa-ma kulluha ayda), sense partly coherent; bayt 2's second half one syllable too long; w18-w20 re-checked on the image.

Read the whole volume for the sender's other ciphers and the circle's tricks: sender re-read as Ibn al-Qubabi (not Ibn al-Qaysarani; not reconciled with qaysarani1350), author of the cipher on 0067-0068; the compiler names lam-alif as one sign, two shapes for one letter, waw+alif nulls at the end, missing dividers and a 'tashifi' type (one sign per letter shape).
Lam-alif as one sign (the compiler's stock formula) instead of the alif sign standing for lam: no sign takes the ligature, and the score is worse.
Tawil scansion with one null alif in bayt 2: both bayts scan, but only about half the text reads as sense; recorded as a candidate, not a reading.

Metre-constrained search (scansearch.py): corpus-derived syllable weights joined against tawil; recovers the second half of bayt 1 but over 100,000 readings of its first half scan, so the metre cannot fix the single-use signs.
Found that another session had read the same cipher in targets/qaysarani1350 (one-to-one key, love verse in tawil); this attempt's homophone hypothesis was wrong. Folder closed as superseded.

outcome.notes: Superseded: the cipher was read in targets/qaysarani1350. This parallel attempt failed (wrong homophone hypothesis); no reading here.
